accepted.s: India recorded coal production of how much in 2024–25, marking the first year in which production exceeded one billion tonnes?
accepted.x: India recorded 1,047.50 MT of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.
accepted.tq: Use the exact production figure and distinguish it from the target and import figures.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s:
With reference to India’s coal sector in 2024–25, consider the following statements:
1. Coal imports declined by 7.9%.
2. Coal imports stood at 243.62 MT.
3. The reduction in imports resulted in savings of about $7.13 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Imports fell by 7.9% to 243.62 MT, producing estimated savings of about $7.13 billion.
accepted.tq: Check whether the percentage, absolute quantity and consequence belong to the same data set.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: What was India’s coal production target for 2025–26?
accepted.x: India’s coal production target for 2025–26 was fixed at 1,157 MT.
accepted.tq: Separate the future target from the previous year’s actual production.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: By August 2025, how much coal production had been achieved against the 2025–26 target?
accepted.x: Coal production by August 2025 was reported as 381.749 MT against the 2025–26 target.
accepted.tq: Match the partial-year achievement with the correct target-year data.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: India ranks where in the world in terms of coal production and consumption, after China?
o: First in production and second in consumption
Third in production and second in consumption
Second in production and third in consumption
accepted.x: India is the world’s second-largest producer and consumer of coal, after China.
accepted.tq: Test the paired ranking without reversing production and consumption.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Coal accounts for approximately what share of India’s commercial energy needs?
accepted.x: Coal meets about 55% of India’s commercial energy needs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the share in commercial energy needs from the higher share in power generation.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Coal India Limited — World’s largest coal producer
SCCL — Planning arm of Coal India Limited
MCL — Government of India’s coal ministry
accepted.x: Coal India Limited is the world’s largest coal producer. CMPDI is its planning arm, while SCCL is a separate coal-producing company.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct organisation-function pairing and reject swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Which of the following is the planning arm of Coal India Limited?
accepted.x: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, abbreviated as CMPDI, functions as Coal India Limited’s planning arm.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional abbreviation rather than the producing subsidiaries.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: How many producing subsidiaries does Coal India Limited have according to the stated organisational structure?
accepted.x: Coal India Limited has seven producing subsidiaries.
accepted.tq: Use the count first, then verify it against the listed entities.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains all the seven producing subsidiaries of Coal India Limited?
o: ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL
ECL, CMPDI, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and SCCL
BCCL, CCL, MCL, SCCL, NCL, WCL and CMPDI
ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, MCL, SCCL and CMPDI
accepted.x: The seven producing subsidiaries are ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL. CMPDI is the planning arm and SCCL is not one of these seven subsidiaries.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure list items and eliminate options containing the planning arm or SCCL.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
accepted.x: SCCL is owned 51% by Telangana and 49% by the Government of India.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed ownership percentages and the swapped governments.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: The SHAKTI policy of 2017 replaced which coal linkage regime?
accepted.x: The SHAKTI policy, introduced in 2017, replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a policy regime from the Acts governing coal allocation and mining.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Under the SHAKTI policy, coal linkages are provided through:
accepted.x: SHAKTI introduced auction or tariff-based bidding for coal linkages in place of the earlier NCDP-2007 regime.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational mechanism associated with the policy rather than its year or parent legislation.
accepted.sec: Production - CIL, SCCL, targets

accepted.s: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions in India began in:
accepted.x: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began in 2020.
accepted.tq: Place the auction mechanism in time against the nearby years of the CMSP Act, SHAKTI policy and later auction rounds.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: After twelve rounds of commercial coal auctions, which of the following was the position regarding mines and peak rated capacity?
accepted.x: After twelve rounds, 134 mines had been sold, with a peak rated capacity of 277.04 MTPA.
accepted.tq: Pair the round count with both the mine count and capacity instead of mixing figures from other stages.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: The 13th round of commercial coal mine auctions opened on:
accepted.x: The 13th round opened on 21 August 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the exact day, month and year to distinguish the auction round from later agreements.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: How many mines were offered in the 13th round of commercial coal auctions?
accepted.x: The 13th round opened with 14 mines.
accepted.tq: Separate the number offered in one round from the cumulative number sold after twelve rounds.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: In the 14th round of commercial coal mine auctions, mines went to:
accepted.x: The 14th round awarded mines to Reliance Industries and Axis Energy.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-owner trap by distinguishing auction awardees from coal-producing public sector entities.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: The agreements in the 14th round were significant because they were the first agreements to include clauses relating to:
accepted.x: The 14th-round agreements were the first to include underground coal gasification clauses.
accepted.tq: Link the special contractual clause with the correct technology rather than with the auction mechanism itself.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: A total of 199 coal mines have been allocated under:
o: The CMSP Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957
The Energy Conservation Act and the Electricity Act
accepted.x: The 199 mines were allocated under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two statutory routes of allocation from the separate linkage policy.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: Which mineral was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral through an amendment to the MMDR framework, enabling the Centre to auction its leases?
accepted.x: Coking coal was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral, allowing the Centre to auction its leases.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific coal variety and avoid substituting the broader category of coal.
accepted.sec: Commercial coal mining - auctions, CMSP Act 2015, MMDR amendments

accepted.s: Coal bed methane is best described as methane that is:
o: Stored only in large underground cavities
Only dissolved in groundwater below coal seams
Produced exclusively by surface combustion of coal
Held in coal seams, partly free in joints and partly adsorbed in micropores
accepted.x: CBM is methane held in coal seams; part of it is free in joints and part is adsorbed in micropores.
accepted.tq: Break the definition into its two storage forms—free gas in joints and adsorbed gas in micropores.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: Commercial recovery of coal bed methane generally involves:
o: Drilling wells and pumping out water
Mining only the surface layer of coal
Burning the coal seam in situ without wells
Injecting only nitrogen into coal seams
accepted.x: CBM is released by drilling wells and pumping out water from the coal seam.
accepted.tq: Match the resource-recovery process with the correct operational steps.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: Coal bed methane is also known as “sweet gas” because it:
o: Has a high concentration of heavier hydrocarbons
Is produced only from sweet-water aquifers
accepted.x: CBM is called sweet gas because it carries few heavier hydrocarbons.
accepted.tq: Use the exact defining chemical distinction instead of interpreting “sweet” literally.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes underground coal gasification?
o: It uses water alone to convert coal into liquid fuel.
It is an in-situ process in which air or oxygen and steam are injected into coal seams to produce syngas underground.
It extracts only methane from micropores without altering the coal seam.
It is an ex-situ process in which coal is transported to a surface furnace.
accepted.x: UCG is an in-situ process. Air or oxygen and steam are injected into the coal seam to produce syngas underground.
accepted.tq: Contrast in-situ and ex-situ processes and identify the correct reactants and product.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: Underground coal gasification is particularly applicable to coal that is:
accepted.x: UCG can be used for deep, thin or unmineable coal seams.
accepted.tq: Identify the resource characteristic that makes underground conversion useful.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: Which of the following is a stated environmental risk of underground coal gasification?
o: Immediate destruction of all surface vegetation
Formation of heavier hydrocarbons in all coal seams
accepted.x: Groundwater contamination is a recognised risk associated with UCG.
accepted.tq: Select the specifically stated risk and reject broader unsupported environmental claims.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.s: What was the position of the MoEFCC expert panel regarding the minimum depth for UCG pilot projects?
o: It refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth.
It waived the 300 m minimum depth.
It increased the minimum depth to 600 m.
accepted.x: The MoEFCC expert panel refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth requirement for UCG pilot projects.
accepted.tq: Watch the NOT-waiver distinction and retain the exact 300 m threshold.
accepted.sec: Coal bed methane and underground coal gasification

accepted.x: Dr M.V.R. Rayalaseema TPP is owned by APGENCO.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s coal supply:
1. Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own.
2. It depends on coal from Singareni and MCL.
3. Its thermal power plants therefore depend entirely on imported coal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and depends on Singareni and MCL; the material does not state that it depends entirely on imported coal.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word “entirely” and distinguish domestic external sources from imports.
accepted.sec: Coal-based thermal plants in AP - location

accepted.s: The ₹37,500-crore scheme currently associated with coal gasification drew:
o: No policy attention during the West Asia conflict
Bids only from Reliance Industries in May 2026
accepted.x: The ₹37,500-crore gasification scheme drew no bids in September 2026. The West Asia conflict nevertheless pushed gasification higher on the policy agenda.
accepted.tq: Separate the policy objective and relevance from the actual response received in the bidding process.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which development pushed coal gasification higher on the policy agenda?
o: The replacement of NCDP-2007 by SHAKTI
The achievement of 1,047.50 MT coal production
accepted.x: The West Asia conflict increased the policy emphasis on coal gasification.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated current-affairs trigger rather than a related coal-sector reform.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Why has the 100 MT coal-gasification goal been viewed with doubt?
o: Because few projects have reached an advanced stage
Because all commercial auctions were cancelled
Because UCG uses only shallow coal
Because coal production crossed one billion tonnes in 2024–25
accepted.x: The 100 MT goal is considered doubtful because few coal-gasification projects have reached an advanced stage.
accepted.tq: Link the criticism to project maturity rather than to total coal production or auction numbers.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures has been recommended by LENS in relation to coal gasification?
1. Use of CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal
2. Zero liquid discharge
3. Mandatory CCUS
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: LENS has called for CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal, zero liquid discharge and mandatory carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS).
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete recommendation set and avoid dropping the environmental safeguards.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: BHEL commissioned the first IGCC plant in:
accepted.x: BHEL commissioned the first Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) plant in 1985.
accepted.tq: Expand the technology abbreviation and associate the correct year with the commissioning event.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First coal mine established at Raniganj
B. BHEL commissioned the first IGCC plant
C. Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began
D. The 13th round of commercial coal auctions opened
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1774, 1985, 2020 and 21 August 2025: A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two intermediate milestones by year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
